    A flat rate charges interest on the full loan for the whole term, even as you repay it. A reducing rate charges it only on what you still owe.

    The starting values are examples, not a quote. Use the rate and tenure from your own loan offer.

    Flat Rate vs Reducing Rate

    With a flat rate, interest is worked out on the original loan amount for the whole tenure. You pay it even on the part of the loan you have already repaid. With a reducing rate, each month's interest is charged only on the balance still outstanding, so it shrinks as you repay.

    That makes a flat rate look cheaper than it is. A 10% flat rate on a five-year loan costs as much as a 17.27% reducing rate, so always compare loans on the reducing rate.

    How to Use This Calculator

    1. Enter the loan amount and the interest rate you were quoted.
    2. Enter the tenure in months: 60 for five years.
    3. Read the reducing rate that a flat rate of that size really costs.
    4. Compare the two columns to see the EMI, total interest and total amount if the same rate were charged each way.

    How the Conversion Is Calculated

    Flat EMI = (P + P × R × N / 1200) / N
    Reducing EMI = P × i × (1 + i)N / ((1 + i)N − 1)

    P is the loan amount, R the yearly rate in percent, N the tenure in months and i the reducing rate / 12 / 100. The equivalent reducing rate is the one at which both EMIs are the same.

    Example: ₹5,00,000 at 10% flat for 60 months has an EMI of ₹12,500 and ₹2,50,000 in interest. The same EMI on a reducing balance means a rate of 17.27%. At 10% reducing, the EMI would be ₹10,624 and the interest ₹1,37,411, which is ₹1,12,589 less.

    What This Calculator Leaves Out

    • Fees: processing charges, GST on fees and insurance are not included. The APR in your Key Facts Statement adds them.
    • Prepayment: paying early changes the interest, and flat-rate loans often refund less of it.
    • Rounding: lenders may round the EMI or the first and last instalments differently.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What is the difference between a flat and a reducing interest rate?
    A flat rate charges interest on the original loan amount for the whole tenure, even though you repay part of it every month. A reducing rate charges interest only on the balance you still owe, so the interest falls as you repay. The same number costs far more as a flat rate.
    How do I convert a flat rate to a reducing rate?
    There is no fixed multiplier, because it depends on the rate and the tenure. For loans of one to five years, the reducing rate is usually about 1.6 to 1.9 times the flat rate: 10% flat over 60 months is 17.27% reducing. The calculator above works it out exactly.
    Which loans in India use a flat rate?
    Home loans are almost always on a reducing balance. Flat rates still turn up on some personal, car, two-wheeler and consumer-durable loans, often from dealers and non-bank lenders. If a quote does not say which it is, ask.
    Is the reducing rate the same as the APR?
    Not quite. The annual percentage rate (APR) also counts fees such as processing charges, so it is usually a little higher than the reducing rate. RBI requires lenders to show the APR in the Key Facts Statement for retail loans, which makes it the best single number for comparing offers.
